Is Wood-Look Flooring the Same as Hardwood? What New Jersey Homeowners Should Know Before Choosing One of the most common questions during flooring consultations in East Brunswick is whether wood-look plank and hardwood are the same thing. They are not, and the difference matters depending on where the floor is going. Hardwood is solid milled wood. It works well in bedrooms and living rooms but cannot handle moisture consistently. Kitchens, bathrooms, and New Jersey basements are risky placements because humidity causes solid wood to expand and contract over time. Luxury vinyl plank is what shows up in most finished renovation photos today. It is waterproof, installs over most existing subfloors including concrete, and comes in realistic wood tones that are difficult to distinguish from the real thing. For rooms that see moisture or heavy foot traffic in Woodbridge, Edison, and Piscataway, LVP is the more practical choice. Pro Tip: If the subfloor has minor imperfections, LVP is more forgiving than hardwood and requires less prep work before installation.

From the owner
Restoration drying vs. insurance company drying — two different things, two very different outcomes. What your insurance company's preferred vendor does: - Prioritizes speed and cost containment on the insurer's timeline - Places standard equipment load and schedules removal on a fixed cycle - Reports findings to the adjuster — not to you What CAMCO does: - Moisture maps the full affected area, not just the visible damage - Adjusts equipment and timeline based on actual readings, not a preset schedule - Documents everything in your interest as the property owner The difference matters most when damage extends beyond the first visible zone — which it usually does. Your insurance pays for restoration. Who performs that restoration is often your choice. Knowing that choice exists is the first step. CAMCO offers free assessments. No obligation. Call us before you assume the insurer's vendor is your only option.

Bathroom remodeling in Davie: two bathrooms the same size can be very different projects, and tile is rarely the reason. What moves the number most is plumbing. Fixtures staying where they are is the biggest saving available in the room. Moving a toilet or a shower drain means cutting the slab, and that changes the schedule and the price together. After that it is the shower. A tub-shower combo is the simplest thing we build. A curbless entry means rebuilding the floor to get the pitch, which is a different project entirely. Honest note: large-format tile means fewer grout lines to clean and a slower install, because the wall has to be dead flat or every seam shows. From the owner
You're lying in bed at 11 p.m., and you can hear your neighbor's TV like it's in your own room. Or maybe you're the one tiptoeing around at 7 a.m., afraid every footstep will wake the people downstairs. Shared walls and floors are the biggest compromise in multi-family living, and most people don't realize how much noise they're signing up for until it's too late. The fix isn't magic, and it isn't cheap. But if you're building or renovating in the Bay Area, there's a practical path forward. We've done dozens of these projects in San Leandro, and the real solution is rarely what people expect. It comes down to decoupling the structure, adding mass, and sealing every gap. Professional installation matters more than product choice for most shared-wall and floor assemblies. And local codes set minimums, but those minimums rarely deliver a quiet living experience. We're a local, family-owned general contractor that's licensed, insured, and bonded. Our team is meticulous, detail-oriented, and honest about what's realistic. We'll help you get the peace and quiet you're after without the surprises. So, what would you do with an extra 300 square feet? Read More https://moderngreenconstructions.com/gallery/

From the owner
Countertops take more daily wear than almost any other surface in the kitchen. Cooking, cleaning, appliances, spills, heat, and constant use can eventually leave an older countertop looking worn even when the rest of the room still looks good. Replacing the countertop can be a practical way for Palmdale homeowners to refresh the kitchen without completely rebuilding it. A new surface can change how the cabinets look, improve the working area, and create a cleaner connection between the backsplash, sink, appliances, and surrounding finishes. Material choice should reflect both appearance and everyday use. Some homeowners prioritize easy maintenance, while others focus more on texture, pattern, or a premium visual finish. Edge details, thickness, sink openings, corners, and seams should also be considered so the finished installation feels clean and intentional. Countertop replacement is often combined with a new backsplash, sink, faucet, cabinet hardware, or lighting for an even stronger transformation. If your current kitchen surfaces are stained, chipped, outdated, or simply no longer match your style, RZ Remodeling can help Palmdale homeowners create a fresher and more functional kitchen environment.
